source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"HUMULIN R may be given subcutaneously; IV administration is permitted under medical supervision with close blood-glucose and potassium monitoring.","B":"HUMULIN R is restricted to subcutaneous use, and intravenous administration is not included in the prescribing information.","C":"Intravenous HUMULIN R can be given without extra monitoring because the route does not change hypoglycemia or potassium-related risk.","D":"Intramuscular HUMULIN R is the preferred labeled route when a faster glucose-lowering response is required in the hospital."}}
source_row.rationale: The current HUMULIN R label includes subcutaneous use and allows intravenous administration under medical supervision with close monitoring of blood glucose and potassium because hypoglycemia and hypokalemia can occur. Option A states the labeled route and monitoring requirements. Option B incorrectly excludes the IV route. Option C removes required monitoring. Option D invents a preferred intramuscular route that is not the labeled hospital alternative described.
source_row.source_detail: DailyMed HUMULIN R (insulin human) — Dosage and Administration, routes of administration: administer subcutaneously; intravenous administration is permitted under medical supervision with close monitoring of blood glucose and potassium to avoid hypoglycemia and hypokalemia. Eli Lilly HUMULIN R FDA label updated 2025-05-27; current DailyMed version live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication routes, administration, reversal, adverse effects/interactions, withdrawal, monitoring and client teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
